answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each agent to post a bond keyed to a hardware-rooted attestation chain, like a repair scheme that must restore the original load path across a mesa of nested trust anchors. Each new identity must present a crystal of countersigned provenance whose signatures chain to a scarce, audited root, so forging one costs the attacker the full bond plus the root's issuance quota. The limit is that a compromised root still mints jade identities, so the design caps blast radius by rate-limiting issuance and forcing periodic re-attestation.
